name: Shackleton–de Gerlache connecting ridge (Artemis III region)
description: A ridge between two craters near the lunar south pole. Parts of it are sunlit most of the year, beside craters in permanent shadow that may hold ice.

sources.illum_pct: Best-lit point near Shackleton rim lit 86% of the year (Bussey et al. 2010, Kaguya topography)
sources.slope_deg: Estimated; Artemis III landing limit <10° over 100 m (NASA Artemis overview, 2025)
sources.temp_swing_C: Estimated from LRO Diviner polar products (the coldest shadowed craters fall below 35 K)
sources.ice_level: Next to permanently shadowed cold traps below 110 K (LRO Diviner)
sources.geology: Highland anorthosite (Unified Geologic Map of the Moon, USGS 2020)

name: Malapert Massif (Artemis III region)
description: The tallest mountain near the lunar south pole. Its height gives it long sunlit periods and a good view of Earth for radio contact.

sources.slope_deg: Estimated; Artemis III landing limit <10° over 100 m
sources.illum_pct: ~74% of lunar year 2020 at Malapert point M1 (54–95% per lunar day), from LOLA-based illumination studies
sources.ice_level: Estimated: polar cold traps in the region (LRO Diviner)

name: Mons Mouton (IM-2 landing, Artemis III region)
description: A flat-topped mountain near the south pole. Intuitive Machines' IM-2 lander touched down here in March 2025, and it was NASA's planned VIPER rover area.

sources.slope_deg: Estimated; plateau top, Artemis III landing limit <10° over 100 m
sources.ice_level: VIPER mission target region for ice (NASA, 2022–2026)

name: Mare Tranquillitatis (Apollo 11 site)
description: A flat plain of dark lava near the Moon's equator, where Apollo 11 landed in 1969.

sources.temp_swing_C: Equator daytime max ~387–397 K, ~95 K before sunrise (Williams et al. 2017, LRO Diviner)
sources.illum_pct: Equatorial: sunlit half of each ~29.5-day lunar day

name: Jezero Crater (Perseverance)
description: An ancient lake basin with a river delta, where NASA's Perseverance rover has been exploring since 2021.

sources.temp_swing_C: Air temperature varies 50–60 °C in a day (Perseverance MEDA, Rodríguez-Manfredi et al. 2023)
sources.surface: Thermal inertia 180–605 (MEDA): mixed sand and rock
sources.wind_ms: Estimated typical wind; MEDA measured gusts ~10 m/s

name: Arcadia Planitia (SpaceX Starship candidates, buried ice)
description: Wide northern plains where SpaceX has imaged candidate Starship landing sites and where ice is likely within a meter of the surface.

sources.ice_level: SWIM ice consistency map, 0–1 m (PSI/NASA JPL, 2025)
sources.slope_deg: Estimated; smooth plains chosen for landing

name: Arsia Mons cave skylights (Tharsis)
description: The flank of a giant volcano with pits that may open into lava tubes. Note: it sits far above NASA's +2 km limit for human landings.

sources.surface: Dusty Tharsis surface, low thermal inertia (THEMIS)
